messages:
maria: quick heads-up — perf run on staging-rt shows KV cache OOMs during continuous batching ramp for mixed short/long traffic. 2 incidents in 3h. logs attached below. :frowning_face:

sam: ugh. are these the same hosts that hit the regressed kernel path from last week?

maria: different hosts. stack: g5x2, model=wizard-13b/q4f16, runtime=1.12.4. OOM trace seems tied to batch admission where we estimate token footprint incorrectly once prefix KV gets large.

jc: can you paste the relevant profiler snippet? especially KV byte counts and batch sizes.

maria: sure — from perf-bot run 2145-03:

```
profile: batch_build
host: g5x2-17
requests: 12 -> formed 3 batches
batch_sizes: [1,4,7]
avg_request_seq: 64
kv_cache_est_bytes(before): 1.8G
kv_cache_real_bytes(after): 3.2G
oom_event: yes (alloc 512MB failed)
note: high prefix reuse on the long reqs, but admission added small seqs and pushed kv footprint over watermark
```

liam: hmm allocation jump from 1.8G->3.2G suggests we double-count or underestimate hidden per-token metadata. our estimator uses tokens * avg_kv_per_token (8 bytes) — that looks low.

anya: plus kernel selection may affect KV layout. when we switch to the fused-attn kernel for long seqs we also enable larger cache entries (aligned buffers). that increases footprint per entry.

sam: proposal: tighten admission policy by adding a token_budget_target per batch and a conservative kv_multiplier when kernel handoff is likely. e.g., if longest_seq > 1024 or switching kernel, multiply kv estimate by 1.8 and cap batch admit accordingly.

jc: agree in principle. we should also prefer batching short requests separately (short-window queue) to avoid dragging long-prefix KV into the same batch. two-queue admission: fast-path (short seq < 128) and mixed-path with stricter token_budget.

maria: I ran a quick sim with the new heuristic: token_budget_target=4096, kv_multiplier=1.75 when any req>1024. results: predicted peak kv 2.5G, no OOM in 1000-sim runs, throughput down ~3% but latency p95 improved for short requests.

perf-bot: [auto] regression-check: baseline 1.12.4 vs heuristic-sim. token cost +0.5%, tokens/sec -2.8%, p95 short-latency -12%. no correctness diffs.

liam: sounds promising. a couple of concerns: 1) handoff detection must be cheap (we only have request metadata before admission). 2) kernel switch decisions currently happen post-admit in executor — we need to predict it deterministically in queue.

anya: we can predict kernel by model config + max_seq_in_batch. the rule: if max_seq_in_batch > 2048 use "large-kernel", if >1024 use "mid-kernel". these thresholds are already used elsewhere. just replicate logic in admission.

sam: action items I propose:
- implement kv_multiplier override in admission policy and expose in runtime config (default 1.0)
- add two-queue gating: short-queue (seq<128) with low token_budget_target, mixed-queue with conservative target
- mirror kernel-selection heuristic in admission to pick kv_multiplier automatically
- add perf test harness to sim mixed traffic and assert no OOM in 10k requests

jc: + add telemetry: emit estimated_kv_before, estimated_kv_after, and kernel_predicted tags for each batch so we can validate in prod without toggling behavior. also emit reason if we reject for kv_pressure.

maria: implementer note: when rejecting we should try to requeue short requests to fast-path immediately instead of outright 429. that should keep PLUX for small interactive calls.

liam: one more nuance: quantized models had smaller per-token KV but larger temporary buffers in fused kernels. we need per-model multipliers. create a per-model default multiplier (e.g., q4f16=1.2, fp16=1.0) and then the kernel predicted multiplier multiplies that.

anya: testing plan: rollout in staged canary with 5% traffic on dedicated pool, capture telemetry for 24h, look for kv_pressure rejects and OOMs. if reject rate <0.5% and no OOMs escalate canary.

sam: can someone sketch the admission pseudo-code?

jc: quick draft:
```
// pre-admission
max_seq = max(req.seq for req in batch_candidate)
kernel_pred = predict_kernel(model, max_seq)
model_base_mult = model_config.kv_multiplier
kernel_mult = kernel_multiplier_table[kernel_pred]
kv_est = sum(req.seq * model_base_mult * token_kv_bytes for req in batch_candidate)
kv_est *= kernel_mult
if kv_est + current_kv_usage > kv_watermark: reject_or_requeue()
else admit()
```

maria: this looks good. what about adaptive token_budget_target tuning? we could slowly increase target if we see low rejection rates and no OOMs, and decrease immediately on any OOM signal.

liam: yes a feedback loop with conservative step sizes. on OOM alert: halve token_budget_target for 10m, then exponential backoff up. record all steps for audit.

perf-bot: [auto] created perf-issue #3467 and staged-run id sr-2145. assigned to @sam and @maria.

anya: I'll take telemetry dashboards: kv_est vs kv_real, reject_rate over time, per-model multipliers, and kernel_pred distribution.

sam: timeline: I'll implement kv_multiplier and kernel mirror in admission this week, add two-queue gating next, then canary next Tue. anyone opposed?

jc: +1. please include unit tests for estimator math (floating vs integer rounding) — that caused a rare off-by-one earlier.

maria: thanks all. saving notes: avoid 429 for short interactive calls, per-model multipliers, kernel-aware kv multiplier, two-queue admission, telemetry. I'll open the RFC PR and link perf logs. :white_check_mark:

liam: cheers.
